questions.q: Certain pairs of words are given, out of which the words in all pairs except one, bear a certain common relationship. Choose the pair in which the words are differently related.
questions.theory:
TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a family tree as you read — never solve in your head. Use symbols: △=male, ○=female, horizontal line=marriage, vertical line=parent-child.
Step 2: Decode nested phrases INSIDE-OUT, one relation at a time. 'My mother's only daughter's father's wife' — start from the innermost: 'my mother' → 'only daughter of my mother' = the speaker's only sister (or the speaker herself, if female with no sisters) → 'father's wife' of that person = the speaker's own mother again (since her father's wife IS the mother).
Step 3: Key vocabulary to fix cold: 'Son of my mother' (with no other clue) = brother (or self). 'Only daughter-in-law of X' = X's son's wife.
Step 4: Once the tree is drawn, the final relationship is just reading one arrow on your own diagram — the hard part is ALWAYS the decoding in Step 2, not the final answer.
Worked Example (real): "Pointing to Q, P said: 'She is the only daughter-in-law of my mother's only daughter's father's wife.' How is P related to Q if P has only one sister?" → 'My mother's only daughter' = P's only sister. 'Her father's wife' = P's mother (P's sister's father IS P's father, and HIS wife is P's mother again). So Q is the 'only daughter-in-law' of P's MOTHER → Q is married to P's mother's only son → that son is P himself (since P has only a sister, no brother). Answer: P is Q's Husband.

questions.q: In a class of 60, where girls are twice that of boys, Kamal ranked seventeenth from the top. If there are 9 girls ahead of Kamal, how many boys are after him in rank?
questions.theory:
TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a numbered line (1 to Total) representing positions left-to-right.
Step 2: Convert every 'from left/right end' clue into a position number using this rule: Position from Left + Position from Right − 1 = Total people. (Memorize this ONE equation — it solves 90% of these questions.)
Step 3: For 'shift left/right by N places' questions: New position = Old position ± N (subtract if shifting left, since position numbers count from the left).
Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.
Worked Example (real): "Rohit is 17th from left end of a row of 29 boys. Karan is 17th from right end. How many boys between them?" → Rohit's position from right = 29−17+1 = 13. Karan's position from left = 29−17+1 = 13. Since Karan (from left=13) is BEFORE Rohit (from left=17), boys between = 17−13−1 = 3.
Ranking (top/bottom) puzzles: Same equation, just replace 'left/right' with 'top/bottom': Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = Total.

Step 1: Draw a family tree as you read — never solve in your head. Use symbols: △=male, ○=female, horizontal line=marriage, vertical line=parent-child.
Step 2: Decode nested phrases INSIDE-OUT, one relation at a time. 'My mother's only daughter's father's wife' — start from the innermost: 'my mother' → 'only daughter of my mother' = the speaker's only sister (or the speaker herself, if female with no sisters) → 'father's wife' of that person = the speaker's own mother again (since her father's wife IS the mother).

TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:

Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.

questions.q: Directions: Read the following information carefully and answer the questions given below: (i) Abhay, Bhanu, Chetan, Devendra, Eishwar, Faizal and Gurnam are sitting around a circle and are facing the centre. (ii) Gurnam is second to the left of Chetan, who is to the immediate left of Faizal. (iii) Abhay is third to the left of Eishwar. (iv) Bhanu is between Devendra and Eishwar. Which of the following is true?
questions.a: Abhay is to the immediate right of Gurnam
questions.theory:
TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a numbered line (1 to Total) representing positions left-to-right.
Step 2: Convert every 'from left/right end' clue into a position number using this rule: Position from Left + Position from Right − 1 = Total people. (Memorize this ONE equation — it solves 90% of these questions.)
Step 3: For 'shift left/right by N places' questions: New position = Old position ± N (subtract if shifting left, since position numbers count from the left).
Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.
Worked Example (real): "Rohit is 17th from left end of a row of 29 boys. Karan is 17th from right end. How many boys between them?" → Rohit's position from right = 29−17+1 = 13. Karan's position from left = 29−17+1 = 13. Since Karan (from left=13) is BEFORE Rohit (from left=17), boys between = 17−13−1 = 3.
Ranking (top/bottom) puzzles: Same equation, just replace 'left/right' with 'top/bottom': Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = Total.

How is P related to Q if P has only one sister?" → 'My mother's only daughter' = P's only sister. questions.q: Forty boys are standing in a row facing the North. Amit is eleventh from the left and Deepak is thirty-first from the right end of the row. How far will Shreya, who is third to the right of Amit in the row, be from Deepak?
questions.theory:
TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a compass cross (N up, S down, E right, W left) and physically sketch the path segment by segment — do not try to track it mentally beyond 2 turns.
Step 2: Turn rules (memorize as a clock-rotation): Facing North, turn RIGHT → now facing East. Turn LEFT → now facing West. The pattern cycles N→E→S→W→N for right turns, and N→W→S→E→N for left turns.
Step 3: For 'shortest distance from start to end' questions: after plotting the full path, use the Pythagoras theorem (a²+b²=c²) on the net horizontal and net vertical displacement — do NOT add up the total path walked.
Step 4 — Shadow logic (sunrise/sunset): In the MORNING, the sun is in the East, so shadows fall to the WEST. In the EVENING, the sun is in the West, so shadows fall to the EAST. If a shadow falls to your right while facing someone, cross-reference with this rule to get your facing direction.
Worked Example (real): "Rock skates 24 km northwards, then turns left and skates 10 km..." → North for 24km, turn left (facing North, left turn → now facing West), skate 10km West. Net displacement: 24km North + 10km West — track each segment on your sketch and sum axis-wise before computing any final distance.

questions.q: In a row of 60 persons, Ganesh is twenty-sixth from left end. Find out his position from the right end.

TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a numbered line (1 to Total) representing positions left-to-right.
Step 2: Convert every 'from left/right end' clue into a position number using this rule: Position from Left + Position from Right − 1 = Total people. (Memorize this ONE equation — it solves 90% of these questions.)
Step 3: For 'shift left/right by N places' questions: New position = Old position ± N (subtract if shifting left, since position numbers count from the left).
Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.
Worked Example (real): "Rohit is 17th from left end of a row of 29 boys. Karan is 17th from right end. How many boys between them?" → Rohit's position from right = 29−17+1 = 13. questions.q: In a row of boys, Kapil is eighth from the right and Nikunj is twelfth from the left. When Kapil and Nikunj interchange positions, Nikunj becomes twenty-first from the left. Which of the following will be Kapil's position from the right?

TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a numbered line (1 to Total) representing positions left-to-right.
Step 2: Convert every 'from left/right end' clue into a position number using this rule: Position from Left + Position from Right − 1 = Total people. (Memorize this ONE equation — it solves 90% of these questions.)
Step 3: For 'shift left/right by N places' questions: New position = Old position ± N (subtract if shifting left, since position numbers count from the left).
Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.
Worked Example (real): "Rohit is 17th from left end of a row of 29 boys. Karan is 17th from right end. How many boys between them?" → Rohit's position from right = 29−17+1 = 13. Karan's position from left = 29−17+1 = 13. Since Karan (from left=13) is BEFORE Rohit (from left=17), boys between = 17−13−1 = 3.

questions.q: Five friends are sitting in a row all facing south. Rani sits immediate right of Mani. Simi sits second to left of Sanu. Jenny sits towards left of Rani. Which of the following statement is correct?
questions.a: Only one person sits between Jenny and Mani

Step 1: Draw a numbered line (1 to Total) representing positions left-to-right.
Step 2: Convert every 'from left/right end' clue into a position number using this rule: Position from Left + Position from Right − 1 = Total people. (Memorize this ONE equation — it solves 90% of these questions.)
Step 3: For 'shift left/right by N places' questions: New position = Old position ± N (subtract if shifting left, since position numbers count from the left).
Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.
Worked Example (real): "Rohit is 17th from left end of a row of 29 boys. Karan is 17th from right end. How many boys between them?" → Rohit's position from right = 29−17+1 = 13. Ranking (top/bottom) puzzles: Same equation, just replace 'left/right' with 'top/bottom': Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = Total.

questions.q: Pointing to Q, P said, "She is the only daughter in law of my mother’s only daughter’s father’s wife." How is P, who is married, related to Q if P has only one sister?
questions.theory:
TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a family tree as you read — never solve in your head. Use symbols: △=male, ○=female, horizontal line=marriage, vertical line=parent-child.
Step 2: Decode nested phrases INSIDE-OUT, one relation at a time. 'My mother's only daughter's father's wife' — start from the innermost: 'my mother' → 'only daughter of my mother' = the speaker's only sister (or the speaker herself, if female with no sisters) → 'father's wife' of that person = the speaker's own mother again (since her father's wife IS the mother).
Step 3: Key vocabulary to fix cold: 'Son of my mother' (with no other clue) = brother (or self). 'Only daughter-in-law of X' = X's son's wife.
Step 4: Once the tree is drawn, the final relationship is just reading one arrow on your own diagram — the hard part is ALWAYS the decoding in Step 2, not the final answer.
Worked Example (real): "Pointing to Q, P said: 'She is the only daughter-in-law of my mother's only daughter's father's wife.' How is P related to Q if P has only one sister?" → 'My mother's only daughter' = P's only sister. 'Her father's wife' = P's mother (P's sister's father IS P's father, and HIS wife is P's mother again). So Q is the 'only daughter-in-law' of P's MOTHER → Q is married to P's mother's only son → that son is P himself (since P has only a sister, no brother). Answer: P is Q's Husband.

Step 3: For 'shortest distance from start to end' questions: after plotting the full path, use the Pythagoras theorem (a²+b²=c²) on the net horizontal and net vertical displacement — do NOT add up the total path walked.
Step 4 — Shadow logic (sunrise/sunset): In the MORNING, the sun is in the East, so shadows fall to the WEST. In the EVENING, the sun is in the West, so shadows fall to the EAST. If a shadow falls to your right while facing someone, cross-reference with this rule to get your facing direction.

Step 3: For 'shift left/right by N places' questions: New position = Old position ± N (subtract if shifting left, since position numbers count from the left).
Step 4: For 'interchange places' questions: after swapping, RE-APPLY the same Left+Right−1=Total equation with the two people's NEW positions swapped.
Worked Example (real): "Rohit is 17th from left end of a row of 29 boys. Karan is 17th from right end. How many boys between them?" → Rohit's position from right = 29−17+1 = 13. Ranking (top/bottom) puzzles: Same equation, just replace 'left/right' with 'top/bottom': Rank from top + Rank from bottom − 1 = Total.

questions.q: Anaya is 15m to the west of Rithika. Rithika is 20m to the north of Genelia. Genelia is 12m to the east of Diksha. Faizah is 16m to the north of Diksha. If Anaya has to meet Faizah through the shortest distance and then has to meet Genelia from Faizah’s point through the shortest distance, then what is the total distance travelled by Anaya?
questions.theory:
TOUGHEST CATEGORY — full method:
Step 1: Draw a compass cross (N up, S down, E right, W left) and physically sketch the path segment by segment — do not try to track it mentally beyond 2 turns.
Step 2: Turn rules (memorize as a clock-rotation): Facing North, turn RIGHT → now facing East. Turn LEFT → now facing West. The pattern cycles N→E→S→W→N for right turns, and N→W→S→E→N for left turns.
Step 3: For 'shortest distance from start to end' questions: after plotting the full path, use the Pythagoras theorem (a²+b²=c²) on the net horizontal and net vertical displacement — do NOT add up the total path walked.
Step 4 — Shadow logic (sunrise/sunset): In the MORNING, the sun is in the East, so shadows fall to the WEST. In the EVENING, the sun is in the West, so shadows fall to the EAST. If a shadow falls to your right while facing someone, cross-reference with this rule to get your facing direction.
Worked Example (real): "Rock skates 24 km northwards, then turns left and skates 10 km..." → North for 24km, turn left (facing North, left turn → now facing West), skate 10km West. Net displacement: 24km North + 10km West — track each segment on your sketch and sum axis-wise before computing any final distance.
